title: resume-friendly streaming consumer API with idempotent reconnects
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: SDK users building streaming chat UIs frequently need robust reconnect semantics that preserve partial responses, avoid duplicate side-effects, and expose simple developer primitives. Current streaming helpers focus on event decoding but leave resume semantics and idempotent reconcilers to application code.

Goal: Provide a small, well-documented consumer API in the Python SDK that: 1) exposes a lightweight Checkpointer/ResumeToken primitive, 2) implements idempotent replays for terminal and incremental events, 3) includes adaptive reconnect/backoff policies and optional at-most-once side-effect guards, and 4) remains ergonomic for both simple clients and advanced integrations (e.g., WebSocket frontends, durable consumer services).

Constraints & non-goals: We will not change server-side contract in this ticket. Assume server emits monotonic resume_token strings in events when resume is supported. This feature is additive and opt-in; default behavior unchanged. Not building "full conversation sync" — only resume and duplicate filtering for a single streaming session stream id.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamingConsumer context manager with optional checkpointer parameter
Resume token from last processed event is persisted via a pluggable Checkpointer interface
Reconnects use exponential jittered backoff and respect configured max_retries
Event deduplication prevents duplicate on_message callbacks for redelivered events
Example in docs shows resuming a chat stream after a transient network flake with no duplicated UI tokens
Unit tests cover reconnect attach/detach, dedupe, and checkpoint persistence failure modes
E2E integration test against staging runtime simulating dropped connections and redelivery

notes:
Design trade-offs considered: 1) server-side vs client-side dedupe: we choose client-side dedupe to avoid changing runtime and to support partial UX recovery; 2) where to surface resume_token: included on every event metadata so SDK can checkpoint mid-stream; 3) default semantics: best-effort resume + at-least-once delivery with dedupe helper, but SDK provides opt-in exactly-once guard using user-provided idempotency hooks.

Example usage (quickstart):

from redwood import StreamingConsumer, FileCheckpointer

checkpointer = FileCheckpointer("/var/tmp/chat_resume_tok")
with StreamingConsumer(model="gpt-x-stream", checkpointer=checkpointer, max_retries=5) as consumer:
    for event in consumer.stream(prompt):
        # event has fields: type, text, resume_token, event_id
        if event.type == "delta":
            ui.append_chunk(event.text)
        elif event.type == "final":
            ui.commit_message(event.text)

Behavior notes:
- On transient disconnect, consumer will attempt to reconnect using a jittered exponential backoff and reattach with last persisted resume_token.
- Redelivered events are filtered by an EventDeduper keyed on event_id and resume_token; the deduper is enabled by default but can be disabled for advanced users.
- If Checkpointer.persist fails, SDK will surface a RecoverableCheckpointError and will continue streaming in-memory; user can configure "stop_on_checkpoint_error=true" to fail fast.

Telemetry: shipped telemetry counters: resume_attempts, resume_success, deduped_event_count, checkpoint_failures. These are tagged by workspace and model for cost/ops analysis.
